## 1. Install Quarto

-   Download and install from <https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/>.\
-   Ensure R is installed if you plan to execute code chunks.\

<iframe src="https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/" width="100%" height="450">

## 2. Create or open a new document

-   Create a new document:
![](img/quarto_newFile.png){width="350"}

-   Basic YAML header:

    ``` yaml
    ---
    title: "Hello Quarto"
    format: html
    ---
    ```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3. Write Markdown & Code Chunks
# 1. Two Main Editing Modes

Quarto lets you choose between a **Visual Editor** and a **Source (Code) Editor**.

## Visual Editor
- WYSIWYG interface similar to a word processor.
- Ideal for those who prefer formatting buttons and live preview.
- Features include toolbar for headings, lists, tables, and inserting code chunks.

## Source (Code) Editor
- Plain-text editing of the `.qmd` file.
- Preferred by users comfortable with Markdown and YAML.
- Works well with version control systems like Git.

> You can switch between Visual and Source modes at any time; both modes save the same underlying `.qmd` text.

---

# 2. Document Structure Elements

Quarto uses **YAML front matter** for metadata and **Markdown** for content.

## YAML Front Matter
Example:
```yaml
---
title: "My Analysis"
author: "Jane Doe"
date: "2025-09-15"
format: html
---
```
- Sets metadata such as title, author, date, and output format.

## Headings
- `#` Level 1
- `##` Level 2
- `###` Level 3

## Lists
- Bulleted list:
  - Item one
  - Item two
- Numbered list:
  1. First
  2. Second

## Code Chunks
````
```{r}
summary(cars)
```
````
- Supports many languages (R, Python, Julia, Bash, etc.).
- Chunk options (e.g., `echo`, `eval`, `fig.width`) modify output.

## Callouts
Create callouts for tips or warnings:
```markdown
::: {.callout-tip}
This is a helpful tip.
:::
```

## Tables
Create simple tables using pipe syntax:
```
| Column1 | Column2 |
|--------:|:-------:|
|   10    |   20    |
```

## Cross-References and Citations
- `@fig-label` for figure references.
- `[@key]` for bibliography citations from a `.bib` file.

---

# 3. Example Document Layout

```markdown
---
title: "Sales Analysis Report"
format: html
---

# Introduction
Brief description…

## Data Preparation
```{r}
library(dplyr)
# your code here
```

## Results
- Key finding 1
- Key finding 2
```

---

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4. Render the Document

-   From the terminal:

    ``` bash
    quarto render hello.qmd
    ```

-   Produces `hello.html` (or PDF/Word if you set a different format).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5. Customize Appearance

-   Use a built-in theme:

    ``` yaml
    format:
      html:
        theme: cosmo
    ```

-   Add custom CSS for branding or typography.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 6. Build Presentations

-   For slides, set:

    ``` yaml
    format: revealjs
    ```

-   Use `##` for new slides, `###` for sub-slides.

-   Render to create an interactive Reveal.js deck.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
